title: the-tester-takes-its-reply-and-cairn-owns-press-office
author: CC (Opus 5), session a187d6ab
intention: The tester takes its own reply in the same bus exchange it opens and disposes of it itself (discard by default, printing crossed/refused per seal), so no reply to the tester ever stands undelivered; and the press_office folder (~/.cairn/folders/press_office, its data recorder) is owned by the cairn device, whose bus already feeds that recorder from the email — the ownership is recorded and the one envelope kind it drops is taken.
how: (1) tester as client: after post() of a seal exchange, the tester reads its personal channel for the reply_to of what it sent (bus.read(to='tester', channel='personal'), the same read shim.py:481 makes), prints crossed/refused per seal from the reply body, records the delivery, and flushes — one exchange, no poll, no second process; a reply the tester does not want is dropped there (record_delivery marks it taken, nothing else is written). (2) a helper on the tester, discard_mail(), that reads and drops every personal envelope addressed to it — the 'it has to be able to do that' — called at the end of every cairn test run. (3) one-time drain of the standing undelivered pile addressed to the tester by a scratchpad script (bus store is instance-space), count on the verdict. (4) press_office ownership: the cairn device's charter owns[] += ~/.cairn/folders/press_office (Akien: 'it can own cairn folders not owned by another device'); the bus (cairn's machine) already feeds the folder recorder (bus.py:208), so nothing is rebuilt — the one undelivered press_office WATCHME envelope is diagnosed and the drop fixed in _try_folder_delivery. (5) proofs: tester tooth under a fixture bus root (undelivered(to='tester') empty after the exchange; refused[] printed); bus tooth (a press_office-addressed WATCHME-kind envelope lands in the folder recorder through _try_folder_delivery); both sealed under netns.
falsifier: DONE when (1) a proof tooth under a fixture bus: the tester posts a seal exchange, codemother's shim replies, and afterwards undelivered(to='tester') is EMPTY and the tester's own record_delivery shows it took the reply (crossed/refused per seal printed) — the tester did the clearing, not the proof; (2) a reply carrying refused[] is printed by the tester at the exchange, never silently stored; (3) the tester discards by default: after a fixture exchange no file under the tester's data_recorder inbound grows unless the tester chose to keep it (a keep is a named choice in code, not the default); (4) the cairn device's charter names ~/.cairn/folders/press_office among what it owns (a folder not owned by another device), through the charter verb of the artifact door, and a tooth shows a press_office-addressed envelope — the WATCHME kind included — lands in the folder recorder through the bus; (5) the standing pile is drained once by a hand (bus store is instance-space) and the count is on the verdict; afterwards a full tester run (cairn test) leaves undelivered(to='tester') at 0. RED if the tester's reply-taking needs a poll, a daemon, or a second process; RED if anything but the tester clears tester mail after the build. WRONG INTENT if Akien wants tester mail kept by default (his words say thrown away).
traces_to: Law 6 (everything has exactly one owner; the tester's mail is the tester's to dispose of, press_office moves under the cairn device through the owner's gate) and Law 7 (a reply carrying refused[] that nobody reads is an error collapsed silently — 13 of them stood). Telos: the bus carries signal, and a pile of 628 undelivered replies is noise the operator inbox counts every session.
watchme: none, because the invariant (no undelivered reply to the tester) is read live every session by cairn/tools/operator_inbox/inbox.py read_email() and asserted by the tester proof tooth at every commit's reseal ladder (cairn/devices/tester/reseal.py); a probe would re-derive the inbox count.

PROVED exit gate — the verdict artifact answers the validate berth's criteria by instrument, including the drained count and undelivered(to='tester') == 0 after a full cairn test run.

decisions.text: SUPERSEDES D1, D2 and D3's owner — applies answered question open-9d1bb9b4d708, Akien 2026-09-23 verbatim: 'All mail generated by tester has to be managed by the testers shim. Period.' and '...they are of no use once the testing is complete. And that they can safely be thrown away.' The taking lives in TesterShim (cairn/devices/tester/shim.py), never in the CLI: no discard_mail() helper, no read-after-post in cli.py.

THE SHIM DISPOSES. TesterShim overrides deliver(envelope): an envelope whose reply_to is non-empty (an answer to something the tester sent) is disposed in the shim and nothing is kept — for each entry of body.refused it prints one line '  refused: <ticket> — <reason>' to stdout (D5), for each entry of body.crossed '  crossed: <ticket>', emits one 'reply_disposed' event (values: reply_to, sender, crossed count, refused count), and returns {'disposed': True, 'reply_to': <id>}. Every envelope with no reply_to goes to super().deliver(envelope) unchanged (bounces, verbs and probe findings keep their paths). BaseShim._check_mail writes the receipt after deliver returns (cairn/tools/base/shim.py, record_delivery by=self.device_id), so the shim's take IS the receipt; nothing else receipts tester mail.

THE EXCHANGE WIRES THE TESTER. In cairn/devices/tester/cli.py the seal announcement's reach becomes reach('codemother', 'harbor_master', 'tester'), so codemother's reply — posted inside post()'s poke chain — is delivered synchronously to TesterShim in this same process. One exchange, no poll, no second process (D1's constraint kept). Nothing else in that block changes; bus.flush() still follows the posts.

THE ONE-TIME DRAIN GOES THROUGH THE SHIM. Measured 2026-10-02 (BusDevice().undelivered): 480 codemother->tester 'sealed reply' envelopes, 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-02. After the build commit CC runs a scratchpad script that does reach('tester') and calls the tester shim's own _check_mail() until undelivered(to='tester') is 0, reading the count before and after; the count goes on the verdict. The drain is the tester disposing its own mail, invoked once by hand — falsifier (5) as written.

D4 SHARPENED, measured 2026-10-02. (a) OWNERSHIP: cairn/devices/cairn/intention+why.json carries no owns field today; the build adds "owns": ["~/.cairn/folders/press_office"] through bin/cairn artifact write <that charter> --verb charter --from <file>, then runs cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/recompile_gate.sh. (b) THE DROP: envelopes c9e5226f (to press_office, the WATCHME kind, 2026-09-30T10:36) and ab8ce962 (to charter) stand undelivered although BusDevice._instance_folder resolves both today. Cause: _try_folder_delivery caches a failed resolution as None in self._folder_recorders for the bus's whole life, and an envelope already stored is never re-offered. Fix, in cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py only: a None resolution is not cached (only a loaded recorder is); and after a folder delivery succeeds, the same call writes that addressee's standing undelivered(to=addressee) envelopes through the same recorder and receipts each with record_delivery(id, to=addressee, by='folder_instanceizer'). The two standing envelopes land on the next post to each addressee.

THE PROOFS, two, each measuring only its own component (RULE 1), committed red before the build and sealed under netns. cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_tester_takes_its_reply.py — PROVES cff5a197b3c4 clauses 1, 2, 3, 5: under a scratch bus with codemother's shim stubbed to reply {crossed, refused}, a seal exchange through reach(..., 'tester') leaves undelivered(to='tester') empty with the receipt by 'tester' (1); refused[] lines are printed (2); the tester's data recorder inbound gains no file (3); a standing pile of fixture replies to 'tester' is disposed by the shim's own drain to 0 (5). cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_folder_mail_lands_late.py — clause 4: the cairn charter's owns names ~/.cairn/folders/press_office, and a scratch folder addressee with no instanceizer at the first post gains one, after which the second post lands both envelopes and undelivered(to=it) reads 0.

D10 LOCATED: the seal announcement is in cairn/devices/tester/cli.py, inside the block after the sealing loop that announces each green seal to codemother; the one line to change reads exactly: bus = reach("codemother", "harbor_master"). It becomes: bus = reach("codemother", "harbor_master", "tester"), with a three-line comment above it naming this ticket. Nothing else in cli.py changes.

D11 SKELETON: the drain is a scratchpad script, not repo code: from cairn.tools.bus_client import reach; bus = reach('tester'); before = len(bus.undelivered(to='tester', limit=100000)); shim = the tester shim reach wired (bus._delivery_hooks['tester'].__self__); loop shim._check_mail(), bus.flush() until bus.undelivered(to='tester', limit=100000) is empty or a pass delivers nothing; print before, after and passes. Those counts go verbatim into the PROVED crossing's why (the verdict). Reach wires the shim, and _wire_delivery already drains the first 50 at wiring.

D12 EXACT: (a) the --from file is a full copy of cairn/devices/cairn/intention+why.json with one key added at the end, "owns": ["~/.cairn/folders/press_office"], written to the scratchpad; the command is bin/cairn artifact write cairn/devices/cairn/intention+why.json --verb charter --why 'cff5a197b3c4: the cairn device owns the press_office folder' --from <that file>. (b) In cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py _try_folder_delivery: read recorder = self._folder_recorders.get(addressee); when absent, resolve and load it, return False WITHOUT caching on a None or a raise, and cache only a loaded recorder. Move the write into a new method _folder_write(recorder, addressee, envelope) that writes the record and then calls self.record_delivery(envelope['id'], to=addressee, by='folder_instanceizer') in place of the bare _ring_delivered.add (that mark is cleared by flush, so the envelope read undelivered again — measured by test_folder_mail_lands_late). On the call that first loaded the recorder, after the current envelope is written, write every other self.undelivered(to=addressee, limit=10000) envelope through _folder_write.

D13: BOTH PROOFS ALREADY STAND, written and run red before this rehearsal: cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_tester_takes_its_reply.py (1/4 green at HEAD: teeth 1, 2, 5 red) and cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_folder_mail_lands_late.py (0/1). They are standalone scripts (python3 <proof>, exit 0 = green) on the pattern of cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_a_requester_takes_its_reply.py. The builder edits neither; the build is done when both exit 0 and are sealed with bin/cairn test --seal <proof> --timeout 900.

D6 ASKS NOTHING OF THIS BUILD. Watching for a specific email is not built, not owed, and not a step: Akien put it 'a long time from now', and when such a test exists its ticket will carry it. A builder reading this ticket does nothing for D6.

D16 EXACT: the write is the same DataRecorder call bus.py _try_folder_delivery already makes, recorder.write({"finding": envelope.get("why", "bus message received"), "inspector_target": addressee, "probe_source": envelope.get("sender", "unknown"), "envelope_id": envelope.get("id"), "verb": envelope.get("verb", ""), "body": envelope.get("body", {})}) — moved verbatim into _folder_write, followed by self.record_delivery(envelope["id"], to=addressee, by="folder_instanceizer") and the existing self.emit("delivered", ...).

D9 EXACT: TesterShim inherits emit from DiagnosticBase through BaseShim (cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py, signature emit(gate, *, pointer=None, values=None)); the call is self.emit("reply_disposed", pointer=envelope.get("id"), values={"reply_to": envelope["reply_to"], "refused": len(body.get("refused") or []), "crossed": len(body.get("crossed") or [])}) where body = envelope.get("body") or {}.

No charter carries a top-level owns today; cairn's is the first. D12 is self-contained: its bus.py half is exactly the _folder_write body D19 spells out, and D19 governs where the two read differently.

D16 is self-contained and governed by D19: the write call is recorder.write(dict) with exactly six keys — finding, inspector_target, probe_source, envelope_id, verb, body — the call bus.py already makes at the current _try_folder_delivery (measured at HEAD), moved unchanged; the charter half is D12's (owns admitted, no schema).

D9 MEASURED at cairn/devices/codemother/shim.py: the sealed reply body is {proof, verdict, crossed, refused, awaiting_hollow}; crossed is a list of ticket-id strings (crossed.append(boat['ticket'])), refused a list of dicts {ticket, reason} (refused.append({'ticket': ..., 'reason': ...})). The tester prints '  refused: <ticket> — <reason>' per refused entry and '  crossed: <ticket>' per crossed string, then self.emit('reply_disposed', pointer=envelope.get('id'), values={reply_to, refused count, crossed count}); emit(gate, *, pointer=None, values=None) is DiagnosticBase's, inherited through BaseShim. D20 restates this and D9 governs.

The drain script prints 'before=<n> after=<n> passes=<n>'; those three numbers are written verbatim into the PROVED verdict's evidence string for the clause-5 criterion (the verdict file the PROVED crossing names, through the chain's verdict door) and into the PROVED crossing's why. The drain is sufficient: reach('tester') wires the TesterShim, whose _check_mail drains up to 50 per call, and bus.flush() between calls clears the ring's delivered set so the anti-join re-reads; loop until undelivered(to='tester') is empty or a pass moves nothing.

measured_at_cast.census: measured 2026-09-16 by BusDevice().undelivered(limit=10000): 628 undelivered envelopes — 619 from codemother, 8 from tester, 1 from press_office (2026-09-15 it read 677: 670 codemother->tester 'sealed reply', 603 of them about /tmp fixture proofs, 13 carrying a refused[] the tester never saw). cairn/tools/base/shim.py:645 posts every verb handler's dict back to envelope['sender'] as a personal '<verb> reply'; the tester is a bus CLIENT (reach/post/flush/exit) whose TesterShim (cairn/devices/tester/shim.py:12) is never wired in its own process, so every reply to it flushes to the store undelivered forever. Default receive() (cairn/tools/base/device.py:244) records delivered mail to ~/.cairn/devices/<dev>/0/tools/data_recorder/inbound/records.jsonl (press_office 116, tester 585, codemother 263, cairn 158 on 2026-09-15) and nothing reads or clears them; all stop 2026-09-13 18:15. press_office is a FOLDER, not a device: measured 2026-09-16 — no cairn/devices/press_office in class-space; ~/.cairn/folders/press_office/instanceizer.json (DataRecorder, first instanceizer tenant, provisioned 2026-09-03 per cairn/tools/instanceizer/intention+why.json) and the bus already activates it from the email: bus.py:208 _try_folder_delivery writes every envelope addressed to a folder into its recorder — ~/.cairn/folders/press_office/data/records.jsonl holds 167 records. The older device-shaped recorder at ~/.cairn/devices/press_office/0/tools/data_recorder/inbound/records.jsonl (117) is the stale path. One press_office->press_office personal envelope (WATCHME kind, 2026-09-15T18:43:59) stands undelivered — the one case the folder delivery did not take.
